section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the three effects of Torah study for its own sake and elaborates on the concepts of peace, the heavenly and earthly retinues, and the building of palaces.
section.t: Rabbi Alexandri said: Whoever engages in Torah study for its own sake makes peace in the heavenly retinue and in the earthly retinue.
Now, in the maamar beginning with these words that was said thirty years ago
(21 Kislev 5701)
it also brings the three opinions
(regarding the effect of engaging in Torah study for its own sake)
that follow
: It is as if he built palaces above and below,
it also protects the entire world,
it also brings the redemption closer.
And it explains in the maamar there,
that peace is the matter of connection
(meaning that there are two separate and distinct matters from each other,
and there is a third that makes peace between them),
and "retinue" (pamalya) means legions,
and in divine service it is the matter of the emotions (midos),
and this is: "Whoever engages in Torah study for its own sake makes peace in the retinue," etc.,
that through engaging in Torah study for its own sake he makes a connection in the emotions.
And it adds in the maamar there: And this refers to the emotions of the heart that are born from the emotions of the intellect
(the intention of this is to explain the two matters in the retinue,
the heavenly retinue and the earthly retinue,
that the heavenly retinue is the matter of the emotions of the intellect,
and the earthly retinue is the matter of the emotions of the heart.
For, behold,
the emotions are the root and source of the creations,
the seven days of construction,
and the intellects (mochin) are above the worlds,
as per the statement
"Two thousand years the Torah preceded the world,"
therefore, in general, the emotions are the aspect of "below" and the intellects are the aspect of "above,"
however, regarding the emotions themselves
(the retinue)
per se,
the emotions of the heart are the earthly retinue and the emotions of the intellect are the heavenly retinue).
And all this is the first effect of engaging in Torah study for its own sake.
And the second effect, "it is as if he built palaces," etc., is
(as explained in the maamar there)
the matter of the intellects,
and also in this there are two levels,
palaces above and palaces below,
the palaces above are the matter of the intellect in the brain,
and the palaces below are the matter of the intellect within the emotions,
as explained in the maamar there.
And this is also what, in the first effect, they said "makes peace in the retinue," etc.
(meaning that the retinue already exists beforehand, and he only makes peace within it),
and in the second effect they said "built palaces," which builds something new,
for the emotions,
since they are the root and source of the creations,
behold they exist in the worlds on their own accord
(and the effect done in them through engaging in Torah study for its own sake is the matter of peace),
but this is not the case with the intellects, which are above the worlds,
behold, the drawing down of the intellects through engaging in Torah study for its own sake is a matter of new building.
And it is known
that the creation of the worlds was for the sake of Yisrael and for the sake of the Torah,
for Yisrael is the matter of Zeir Anpin,
the emotions
(and as is known
that Yisrael is an acronym for "Yesh Shishim Ribo Osios LaTorah" (there are six hundred thousand letters to the Torah),
and it is known
that the number six hundred thousand is from the aspect of the emotions,
a vav being comprised of a yud, and a yud of a yud, etc.)
and Torah is the matter of the intellects,
and from this it is understood that through the two aforementioned effects accomplished through engaging in Torah study for its own sake
[makes peace in the retinue, etc.,
the aspect of emotions
(Yisrael),
and built palaces, etc.,
the aspect of intellects
(Torah)],
afterwards it also comes into the world that was created for the sake of Yisrael and for the sake of the Torah.
And this is the matter of the third effect
"it also protects the entire world,"
and as stated in the maamar: that the intellects and emotions protect the world, these being the actions performed through the attainment of the intellect and the emotions of the heart.
However, this effect that is done in the world,
that the intellects and emotions
(the aspects of Torah and Yisrael)
protect it,
is the perfection of the world as it is from the aspect of creation,
for the beginning of the world's creation was for the sake of Yisrael and for the sake of the Torah, as above,
however, the fourth effect of engaging in Torah study for its own sake,
"it also brings the redemption closer,"
is the matter of a perfection that is above the matter of creation,
and as stated in the maamar: that it changes in its very essence, etc.
And as is known
in the explanation of the Sages' statement
"All 'toldos' (generations/offspring) in Scripture are spelled deficiently, except for two: 'Eileh toldos hashamayim v'ha'aretz' (These are the generations of the heavens and the earth)
and 'V'eileh toldos Peretz' (And these are the generations of Peretz),
for although both of them are spelled fully,
nevertheless there is a great difference between them,
that "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth" is the matter of the aspect of perfection as it is from the aspect of creation,
but this is not the case with "And these are the generations of Peretz,"
the matter of the redemption,
it is an aspect of perfection that is above the matter of creation.
